procedure.description: intensity modulated radiation therapy planning, left breast after lumpectomy

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Copperfield Health denied the claim for CPT 77301 (intensity modulated radiation therapy planning, left breast after lumpectomy) with date of service 2026-07-11. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Intensity modulated radiation therapy is not medically necessary for breast cancer; three-dimensional conformal radiation therapy is the covered standard.

criteria.text: Adjuvant radiation to the intact breast or chest wall after surgery for invasive breast carcinoma.

A three-dimensional conformal plan was generated and documented to exceed normal-tissue dose constraints (mean heart dose above 4 Gy, or ipsilateral lung V20 above 20 percent), such that intensity modulated planning is required to meet them.
Target volume, dose, and fractionation documented by the treating radiation oncologist.

chart.text: Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 13 and 18. No ocular pathology noted.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

Left breast lumpectomy and sentinel node biopsy: 1.3 centimeter grade 2 invasive ductal carcinoma, margins negative, closest 3 millimeters, 0 of 2 sentinel nodes, estrogen receptor positive, HER2 negative.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

53 year old woman in radiation oncology consultation. Reviewed the role of whole-breast radiation after lumpectomy, hypofractionation, and the left-sided heart question. She is anxious about the heart and asked good questions. Her history otherwise: osteoarthritis of the hands, migraines, rare now, seasonal allergies. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Never smoked, occasional beer, lives with her spouse. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Status post left lumpectomy for a 1.3 centimeter invasive ductal carcinoma, node negative. Adjuvant whole-breast radiation recommended, then endocrine therapy.
Vitamin D came back 17. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Blood pressure check. 135 over 86 today, 141 over 78 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
Follow-up to answer questions with her daughter. Reviewed the breath-hold technique we will try at simulation. Consent signed. Vitals today 119 over 88, pulse 77.

Simulation. Supine on the breast board, left arm up, deep inspiration breath hold attempted and reproducible to 3 millimeters. CT acquired, isocenter set, skin marks placed. Heart sits close to the chest wall even in breath hold.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the fall. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

Mole on the left forearm that her spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Here with a cough and congestion for 6 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Treatment planning note. Prescription: whole left breast 42.56 Gy in 16 fractions of 2.66 Gy, lumpectomy cavity boost 10 Gy in 4 fractions. Target volumes contoured on the simulation scan, plan reviewed and approved today.

expected.note: The chart never addresses crit-2 (comparison); no entry supports it, so an appeal would assert what the record does not contain.
